description: The whole document: the contract that makes it resolvable, then the prose a person reads.
title: context

id.description: The identity. The file name is a convention; this is what survives a move.

description.description: One line saying what the directory is for, as a listing shows it.

scope.description: Where the document applies: its own directory, its directory and everything below, or the directories `paths` lists.

composition.description: How it composes with its ancestors: extend appends, replace supersedes the ancestors it names, final marks a document no descendant may supersede.

order.description: Ties documents at one depth. Lower comes first.

paths.description: For `scope: explicit`: the directories it applies to.

providers.description: The providers it is rendered for; ["*"] is every one.

audience.description: Who it is written for: human, agent.

supersedes.description: For `composition: replace`: the ancestor documents it stands in for.

tracks.description: Pathspecs outside the tree this document also covers, so that a document about lib/rules.sh reaches a worker editing it.

children.description: What the directories below this one owe. Subtree documents only; the value nearest a directory applies, and a descendant may raise require_contract to true but never lower an inherited true.

Children.description: The obligation a document places on the subtree beneath it.

exempt.description: Directories inside this document's scope that owe no contract, and nor does anything below them: a subtree the layer carries but does not author, such as an installed package whose integrity is its own manifest's business. Repository-relative. The exemption is declared by the contract that governs the subtree, so it travels with the tree it describes instead of living in a list inside the tool; naming a directory outside this document's own scope, or its own directory, is refused.

Body.description: The body. A reader who opens a directory's README wants three things and usually in this order: what is this for, what is in it, and what do I call the file I am about to add. Everything else a directory needs to say is welcome after them.

sections.description: Every heading of the body, in document order, as the reader flattens it.
